gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 30?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Met Office and supporting models indicate a daily maximum of 22°C in London on August 31, 2026, under breezy conditions with early cloud breaking to sunny spells and scattered light showers around midday that fade westward.** 

These conditions, driven by Atlantic low-pressure influences and moderate westerly winds, limit daytime heating while preventing significant overnight radiative cooling. Historical late-August baselines for London average highs near 20–21°C, so current guidance sits slightly above normal but constrained by cloud cover and precipitation timing. 

Model runs show broad agreement on peak values in the 21–23°C range, with limited potential for brief clearing to push toward 24°C or persistent showers holding it at 21°C. Market-implied probabilities (22°C at 48.5%, 23°C at 34%) closely track this consensus, reflecting trader assessment of official guidance and typical model spread for the resolution criteria of the recorded daily high. No sharp forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and other models point to a maximum temperature near 28–31°C in Tokyo on August 31, 2026, under mostly cloudy skies with light easterly winds and limited sunshine.** This setup follows cooler conditions on August 30 (official max 27.5°C at Tokyo), when stronger cloud cover and a post-frontal airmass suppressed heating. 

Persistent marine influence from the east, combined with high humidity and a chance of scattered light showers or drizzle, is expected to cap daytime warming and prevent a rebound to typical late-August peaks near 30–32°C. Model consensus favors a peak around 28–29°C, aligning with the market’s heaviest positioning on those outcomes, while lower probabilities on 30°C+ reflect the limited upside from reduced insolation. 

Traders appear to weigh the JMA’s latest guidance and real-time observations against historical August variability, where brief cool spells can keep daily maxima 2–4°C below climatology when cloud cover persists. No major model shifts have emerged in the past 24 hours that would materially alter these implied probabilities before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models indicate a mostly cloudy day with a high near 30–31°C for Tokyo on September 1, driven by lingering summer warmth ahead of an approaching frontal system that increases cloud cover and scattered shower chances by afternoon. This transitional pattern, typical for early September when the seasonal shift from Pacific high pressure begins, aligns closely with the 1991–2020 climatological normal of 30.0°C and explains the tight clustering of trader-implied probabilities around 29–31°C. Model spreads remain modest given the short lead time, though minor variations in timing of any onshore flow or insolation could shift the peak by 1°C; updated runs tomorrow will refine resolution criteria for the daily maximum recorded at the Tokyo observation site.
